brief: The Fed raised its policy rate 25bp to 3.75-4.00% (12-0 unanimous), in line with SEB's, consensus and market expectations, to support "a timelier return" to the 2% target, which SEB reads as mainly preserving credibility after prolonged high inflation. Warsh called the move "removing a dose of accommodation" and said members now widely share his Jackson Hole view that financial conditions are not restrictive, but the median rate projections, which exclude Warsh, point to more tightening: at least one more hike this year and possibly another in 2027. This challenges SEB's prior view of a single credibility-boosting hike. Warsh cited three factors behind the September move versus July: a strengthening labour market, inflation not having "passed the test," and geopolitics affecting commodity prices. SEB expects continued 2026 hikes unless inflation clearly improves or growth and labour weaken, but sees a hike at the October 27-28 meeting, just before midterm elections, as unlikely. The market reaction was hawkish: 2-year yields rose 13bp and 10-year yields rose 7bp to back above 5%, equities fell, the dollar strengthened, and pricing moved to roughly 50% odds of an October hike and at least three total hikes by next summer.
